title: Pilot study evaluating an artificial-intelligence-assisted telephone-based pre-consultation history taking to improve clinical workflow and quality of care
summary:
In specialised university outpatient clinics, patients often wait a long time for an appointment. One reason is that a substantial part of the appointment is spent collecting and documenting standard information, for example medication, allergies, previous illnesses and family history.

This study examines whether an additional telephone conversation before the appointment is helpful. During this conversation, a voice-based, AI-assisted system collects this basic information by telephone. The system does not provide diagnoses, does not give recommendations and does not make decisions. The information collected is made available to the physician before the appointment as preliminary information and is reviewed during the consultation.

Adults who already have a first scheduled appointment at a university outpatient clinic can take part. They are randomly assigned to one of two groups: with or without the telephone conversation beforehand. The main comparison is the time required for the consultation and its documentation. In addition, participant satisfaction and physician feedback are recorded.

A total of 100 participants are planned. The additional time required is approximately 20 minutes for information and consent, approximately 30 minutes for the telephone conversation in the intervention group, and approximately 10 minutes for a short questionnaire after the appointment. No additional physical examinations are performed and no biological samples are taken. Medical care is independent of study participation and remains unchanged. Participation is voluntary and can be withdrawn at any time, without giving reasons and without any disadvantage.
conditions: Not disease-specific. The study investigates a care process rather than a disease. The target population comprises adult patients with a scheduled first presentation at a university outpatient clinic.

interventions.name: Intervention group: standard care plus an additional AI-assisted, voice-based history taking by telephone prior to the scheduled outpatient appointment. The system collects basic history information in a structured manner only. It does not provide diagnoses, treatment recommendations or clinical dec

Control group: standard care without AI-assisted pre-consultation history taking. History
taking and documentation are performed during the regular outpatient appointment as usual. No additional study-related examinations are performed.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age 18 years or older.
2. Scheduled first presentation (first physician contact) at a university outpatient clinic.
3. The scheduled outpatient appointment is at least 7 days in the future, allowing sufficient time for information, consent and the pre-consultation history taking.
4. Sufficient German language skills to complete the questionnaires.
5. Reachable by telephone and able to take part in a telephone-based history taking.
6. Capacity to consent and written informed consent obtained.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Acute emergency or urgent presentation.
2. Relevant hearing, speech or communication impairment preventing a valid telephone-based assessment.
3. Lack of capacity to consent or absence of valid informed consent.
4. Cancellation or change of the scheduled outpatient appointment, or inpatient admission before the scheduled appointment.
5. Not reachable by telephone or unable to take part in the telephone-based history taking.
6. Explicit refusal of any involvement of artificial intelligence in the history taking.
